intro: Claude Code has a file-based memory system. Memories persist across sessions — loaded automatically every time you start a session in a project.

sections.title: Memory File Format
sections.code:
---
name: Feedback: terse responses
description: User wants short, direct responses with no padding
type: feedback
---

No trailing summaries after tool use. No 'I've completed...' closings.
One sentence updates during work.

**Why:** User finds verbose responses slow and distracting.
**How to apply:** Every response — check length before sending.

items.title: Ask Claude to remember
items.body: Say 'Remember that we use cursor-based pagination everywhere — add this to memory.' Claude writes the file and updates the index automatically.

items.title: Ask Claude to recall
items.body: Say 'Check your memory for context about this project before we start.' Claude reads the index and surfaces relevant memories.

items.title: Memory goes stale
items.body: Memories can be wrong after refactors. Before acting on recalled memory, Claude should verify against the current code. Trust what you see — not what was remembered.

items.title: What NOT to store
items.body: Don't store code patterns (read the code), git history (use git log), in-progress task details (use task list), or things already in CLAUDE.md.
